# Retained player creation and persistence acceptance

The reproduction driver copies the latest player's domain, formal build,
snapshot, and selected conversation into an independent hidden test profile.
Original files and databases are read only. Scheduled tasks must be absent;
the credential store is not copied. The sealed application executes the real
Godot PCK and dispatches the existing protected interact action. Bound images
and before/after snapshots record whether pickup actually occurred.

The natural follow-up driver restores the same conversation through normal
F2 presentation and uses the original Composer callbacks. Before input and
send it verifies the selected session. The original model, thinking level,
and permission mode are retained. Credentials needed by the isolated copy
are installed through the normal provider API, followed by a normal restart.
It does not manually accept permissions, check, adopt, or alter generated code.

No extra model-call, token, repair-round, or whole-run deadline is imposed.
A cancellation file and signals stop the run normally. Transport timeouts
remain distinct from model budgets. Errors and intermediate failed attempts
are retained, including execution-path limits and pre-model TURN_ENDED.

Only a different formal build, actual automatic handoff, and save/reopen can
complete a modification-flow report. Generated gameplay still needs separate
actual interaction evidence; a build check or model statement alone is not
proof that E pickup, equipment, or persistent ammunition works.

The prompt-response diagnostic wraps the existing main IPC handler only to
record its returned error. It forwards the original arguments and result,
does not modify authorization, and runs only in the isolated hidden owner.

Validation at this commit: both driver syntax checks passed; sealed 125f
reproduction confirmed failed pickup at 0.726 metres with actual interact
dispatch and a clean native exit. Subsequent ordinary modification wrote
revision 6, but path-length and then TURN_ENDED preconditions prevented its
adoption. Those failures remain preserved, not presented as passed gameplay.
